name: Facet
text: Default to system preference for theme, with a persistent manual override toggle. This keeps the interface adaptive and reduces friction for users who prefer their OS settings, while the toggle ensures accessibility for those who need high contrast or dislike dark themes. The trade-off is slightly more complex settings management, but it’s worth it for universal comfort and speed of use.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The real risk isn’t preference—it’s habituation. Users won’t switch from dark mode if it’s the default, even when light mode would help them see better. A better alternative: start with system preference, but log the override choice and prompt users to reconsider after 30 days. Settle it with A/B testing: measure task completion time and error rates in both modes.

name: Facet

This forces habituation to break and prevents users from staying stuck in a suboptimal theme. The trade-off is a one-time disruption for long-term clarity and accessibility gains.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The real risk is *false habituation*—users who override once won’t revisit the toggle, locking them into a theme that may no longer suit their needs. Better: log overrides permanently, but don’t auto-switch; instead, highlight the toggle in the settings panel after 30 days with a clear reason—“Your last override was 30 days ago. Reconsider?” Settle it with a 5-user usability test: if 3 out of 5 switch back after the nudge, the nudge works.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Default to system theme on first load, cache the last manual toggle, and after 30 days of no override, highlight the theme toggle in settings with a clear prompt to reconsider—owned by Facet.
